subject: Request: carve-out for runtime filter/tool-call degradations impacting structured outputs
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: production incidents - tool-call/content filter failures (logs attached)

Hi Soojin,

Quick summary: over the last 36 hours we've seen 0.8% of calls to your tool-calling surface get rejected by content filters and ~1.6% return malformed structured outputs (missing JSON fields). When that happens our ingestion job retries and sees higher tail latency (p95 jumps to ~1.2s per request) and queued backpressure. We've attached a condensed runtime error log.

This is causing spikes in our downstream ETL and a couple of dashboarding pipelines failed their SLAs this morning. We understand filtering is necessary, but given this is a production workload with committed throughput we need a formal carve-out (exception) to Redwood's standard uptime/latency SLA for failures attributable to content filtering and structured-output parsing errors so we can align our retries and timeouts.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can:
- Accept responsibility for classification/filter-origin incidents and commit to a clear mitigation timeline, or
- Offer an SLA exclusion language we can present to our procurement/security team that limits customer liability during filter-triggered degradations.

Thanks — attaching the two exported logs.

Attachment: acme_runtime_error_log_20260118.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Liam
Platform Reliability — Acme Corp

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production incidents - tool-call/content filter failures (logs attached)

Liam — thanks for the detailed log and the callout. We see the same error clusters in our observability and I pulled the initial traces. Short answers up front: yes, we own the behavior of our hosted content filters and will treat filter-origin failures as a distinct incident class for enterprise customers; however, formal carve-out language needs Product + Security signoff.

Next steps we propose:
- I'm opening an internal incident and tagging Product/Security.
- We'll produce a draft carve-out clause by EOD that scopes: filter-triggered rejections, malformed structured outputs from tool-calls, and automatic fallback routing failures.
- In parallel, our team will provide recommended client-side retry/timeouts to avoid excessive queuing (we'll include sample backoff settings).

Cc'ing Neha (security) and Rishi (account lead). Can you confirm whether Procurement needs the carve-out to be limited to a time-window (e.g., incidents tied to a deployment) or permanent language in the SLA?

— Soojin
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for runtime filter/tool-call degradations impacting structured outputs

Team — quick notes from Security's perspective:
- We need to keep content filtering in place for compliance; carve-outs should not permit bypassing filters.
- Carve-out language should therefore be scoped narrowly:
  * Definition of "filter-origin failure": classification false-positives that lead to request rejection, and server-side serialized output not matching declared structured schema.
  * Limitations: carve-out only for customer liability/credits; it must preserve Redwood's obligation to remediate and to provide logs for audits.
- Ask Product (Marissa) for the operational mitigation timeline expectations (time-to-first-fix, mitigations, and monitoring hooks).

I'll review the draft SLA clause.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for runtime filter/tool-call degradations impacting structured outputs

Attached is an internal draft carve-out I put together. High-level approach:
- Carve-out applies when our routing/serving stack determines the root cause is our content-filtering module or the tool-calling/structured-output serialization chain (we'll tie this to trace ids).
- Remedies: credit schedule tied to incident severity + mandatory post-incident report with remediation plan within 48 hours.
- Customer-facing guidance: recommended client timeouts (client-side 2s p95 target, exponential backoff starting 200ms) and a strong suggestion to enable idempotent job semantics.

Attachment: proposed_sla_carveout_20260118.pdf (PDF, 18 pages)

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acme.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for runtime filter/tool-call degradations impacting structured outputs

Thanks — a few clarifications from Procurement/Security at Acme:
- Procurement prefers permanent SLA language rather than a per-incident addendum.
- Security needs the ability to request retained evidence for up to 12 months for incidents classified as "filter-origin failures."
- One ask: can Redwood include a non-repudiation attest that filter policy changes that cause regressions will be communicated 24 hours prior to rollout (or a rollback window)?

We looked quickly at your draft and will compile comments.

Sarah Gomez
Senior Contracts Manager — Acme Corp

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>, Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 17:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for runtime filter/tool-call degradations impacting structured outputs

Thanks all — finalizing next steps here and attaching the formal carve-out draft for Acme's review. Quick commitments from Redwood:
- We will treat "filter-origin failures" as a defined incident class and provide credits per the draft schedule when root cause is our filter/serialization chain.
- Redwood will deliver a post-incident report within 48 hours and retain related evidence for 12 months (per Acme's ask).
- We will add a policy: for non-critical filter policy changes, we will provide a 24-hour rollout notice and a one-hour automatic rollback window if regression signals appear. Critical/urgent changes needed for compliance or safety may be exempt but will be reviewed by Security with Acme during the incident report.

Please review the attached PDF and provide redlines. If acceptable, I'll route to Legal to produce formal contract language and share a DocuSign link.

Attachment: proposed_sla_carveout_20260118.pdf (formal draft for external review)

— Soojin
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
